context:
Start from measurement, not intuition. Use the existing marker census and
`scripts/analyze_test_timings.py` to capture the current fast-lane contents,
slowest selected tests, and startup-heavy files. Then tighten the default
policy in `tests/conftest.py` so unclassified tests land in `medium` unless
there is a specific reason they belong in `fast`.

After the default policy changes, audit every explicit `@pytest.mark.fast`
usage across `tests/unit` and `tests/integration`. Reclassify tests based on
actual behavior: subprocess/CLI startup, benchmark data generation, heavy
imports, table-format dependencies, cloud-adjacent fixtures, and expensive
file or database setup should move out of `fast`. Keep `fast` for true smoke
and lightweight developer-loop coverage.

Finish by updating command expectations and adding an automated guardrail that
checks both composition and runtime budget so future test additions cannot
silently re-inflate the fast lane.
description:
The current pytest fast lane no longer behaves like a lightweight developer
suite. On 2026-03-07, `uv run -- python -m pytest -m "fast" --tb=short`
selects 13,256 of 15,051 collected tests and produces a visible 10-30 second
system lock-up during startup under the default parallel settings.

The root cause is classification drift, not a single broken test. The marker
policy in tests/conftest.py currently defaults most unclassified unit tests to
`fast`, so recent testing improvements silently expanded the fast lane far
beyond its intended scope. This interacts badly with pytest-xdist startup and
heavy import/setup work, but parallel execution itself is not the problem and
must be preserved for the curated fast lane.

This TODO restores the original intent of the fast suite by performing a
comprehensive reclassification of tests, tightening default marker policy,
preserving parallel fast execution, and adding guardrails so the lane cannot
quietly bloat again. The outcome target is a truly lightweight parallel fast
suite aligned with the prior expectation that fast runs stay under roughly
80 seconds.

anti_patterns.instead: keep parallel execution and reduce the lane size.
anti_patterns.why: that hides the classification regression instead of fixing it

anti_patterns.dont: move expensive tests out of fast without preserving another routine lane that still covers them
anti_patterns.instead: keep them reachable through `medium`, `slow`, `stress`, or `resource_heavy` workflows.

anti_patterns.dont: rely on a small hand-maintained exception list alone
anti_patterns.instead: add a maintained inventory and validation guardrails.
anti_patterns.why: new tests will keep drifting into `fast`
many unit tests have heavy startup, subprocess, import, or data-generation costs

deferrals.reason: Worker tuning is secondary. The primary fix is to shrink and curate the fast lane without removing parallelism.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: xdist worker-count tuning explicitly called secondary to the primary fast-lane curation fix; no standalone need signal.
deferrals.summary: Tune xdist worker counts or pytest startup internals after reclassification

deferrals.reason: This item is focused on restoring the fast suite and adding guardrails, not a full marker-system redesign.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Full test-taxonomy redesign beyond fast/medium/slow/stress/resource_heavy was explicitly out of scope for the parent restoration effort; no driver to revisit now.
deferrals.summary: Redesign the entire test taxonomy beyond fast/medium/slow/stress/resource_heavy

preserves.behavior: Broad unit coverage remains available through existing non-fast commands such as `test-unit`; reclassification must not hide tests from routine quality workflows.
Existing explicit slow, stress, and resource_heavy coverage remains runnable after reclassification.
The resource-heavy/stress split in `test-all` continues to protect machines from known heavyweight suites.
`uv run -- python -m pytest -m "fast" --tb=short` remains a parallel run; do not force `-n 0` as the primary fix.

verifications.description: Confirm the curated fast lane remains parallel and completes within budget after implementation
verifications.expected: Fast suite runs in parallel without the prior startup lock-up and returns to an acceptably lightweight runtime, targeting the historical sub-80-second budget.

verifications.description: Confirm broad unit coverage is still available outside the fast lane
verifications.expected: Unit tests remain broadly selectable even after fast-lane pruning.

work_units.summary: Capture the current fast-lane baseline, marker census, and startup hot spots
Change default marker policy so unclassified tests no longer auto-enter the fast lane
Reclassify explicit fast-marked tests in tests/unit using measured runtime and startup behavior
Reclassify explicit fast-marked tests in tests/integration and any remaining non-unit fast coverage
Replace drifting path exceptions with a maintained classification inventory for medium, slow, stress, and resource-heavy coverage
Update developer commands and marker-validation tests to match the curated fast-lane contract while keeping parallel execution
Add regression guardrails that fail when fast-lane size, composition, or runtime exceed budget
Verify the final fast lane against the historical runtime target and document the new classification boundaries
